paper_metadata.title: Call Option Pricing Using Quantum Amplitude Estimation: A Comparative Study with Monte Carlo Simulation

summary: The paper implements Iterative Amplitude Estimation (IAE) for European call option pricing using 3–4 qubits on IBM's ibm_brisbane and Qiskit simulators. QAE achieved ~0.008 absolute error relative to the Black–Scholes benchmark with 16 iterations and 2000 shots, comparable to Monte Carlo (error ≈0.0077) but with wider confidence intervals (≈0.015 simulator, ≈0.029 hardware vs ≈0.0026 for Monte Carlo). The study demonstrates feasibility but only theoretical quadratic speedup O(1/ε) over Monte Carlo’s O(1/ε²).

experiments.description: Iterative Amplitude Estimation (IAE) for European call option pricing, evaluated on Qiskit simulator and IBM Quantum hardware, compared against Monte Carlo and Black–Scholes benchmarks.

algorithm.variant: Iterative Amplitude Estimation (IAE) for option pricing

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Log-normal distribution of terminal asset price S_T discretized over [L,H] covering three standard deviations of the log-normal mean; encoded into an n-qubit register. Payoff encoded into an ancilla qubit via controlled rotations.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Price a European call option: C = e^{-rT} E[(S_T-K)+] under risk-neutral GBM dynamics.

problem_instance.description: European call option pricing under geometric Brownian motion with log-normal terminal asset distribution.

dataset_specification.preprocessing: Discretize terminal log-normal distribution over interval [L,H] covering three standard deviations; normalize probabilities; scale payoff for amplitude encoding

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Sample Z ~ N(0,1), generate S_T = S0 exp((r - 1/2 sigma^2)T + sigma sqrt(T) Z) for Monte Carlo baseline; for QAE, discretize the log-normal distribution and normalize probabilities for amplitude encoding.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compare QAE estimates against Monte Carlo and Black–Scholes; report absolute error, relative error, 95% confidence intervals, runtime/resources; simulator uses 2000 shots and 16 IAE iterations; hardware run on ibm_brisbane.

noise_model.noise_type: hardware noise / gate errors / qubit noise / discretization effects

implementation_details.classical_solver: Monte Carlo simulation and Black–Scholes analytical formula as baselines
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Monte Carlo baseline with N=100,000 trials and fixed random seed; QAE simulator with Qiskit Aer Sampler.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Clopper–Pearson intervals used in IAE; option price recovered as C = e^{-rT} a B.

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: iterative amplitude estimation with increasing Grover powers

speedup_claims.conditions: Iterative Amplitude Estimation (IAE) for expectation estimation in option pricing
speedup_claims.caveats: Claimed asymptotic advantage O(1/ε) vs O(1/ε^2); hardware noise, discretization, and limited qubit depth reduce practical gains.

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not reported; likely very large due to amplitude-loading overhead and NISQ noise.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Large fault-tolerant quantum computer capable of deep amplitude encoding circuits and many Grover iterations; substantially more qubits than the 3–4 used here plus error-corrected logical qubits.
limiting_factors: Hardware noise on ibm_brisbane widening confidence intervals (~0.029)
Amplitude encoding and payoff circuits increase depth
Classical Monte Carlo provides tighter confidence intervals (~0.0026)

notes: num_qubits reported as 3-4 qubits for hardware-friendly setup; 3 qubits recorded as the explicit lower bound because the paper states 3–4 qubits and does not give a single fixed register size for all runs.
circuit_depth not explicitly reported; only max iterations = 16 and reduced circuit depth are mentioned, so depth is null.
hardware.type reported from IBM Quantum hardware (ibm_brisbane), a superconducting gate-based device.
Monte Carlo and Black–Scholes are classical baselines, not separate experiments.
Paper claims theoretical quadratic speedup of QAE over Monte Carlo but experimental results do not show practical advantage.
Classical Monte Carlo achieves narrower confidence intervals and similar or better accuracy in reported experiments.

experiments.description: Iterative Amplitude Estimation (IAE) for European call option pricing executed purely on a Qiskit Aer simulator to evaluate algorithmic performance without hardware noise.
